chapter: Sharkey, Chicago and the hot men
title: The original Dixieland band in Chicago and Lawrence Vega
summary: Who played trumpet with Johnny Stein and Yellow Nunez in Chicago (Nick LaRocca, Raymond Lopez) and Lawrence Vega, one of three hot men in town.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And that he wanted to play a clarinet. No. I think you're right. They couldn't afford a clarinet, but they got him a trumpet. And then one guy who later became famous with some man up in Chicago, who was the trumpet man there? I can't remember. He still left. Left and they couldn't get nobody else until he started playing trumpet. That's right. That's out. Who was the trumpet player with the Johnny Stein and Yellow Nunez band up there in Chicago? The original, original Dixie. Nicola Rocca. Was that Lopez? Nicola Rocca.
No, not Raymond. Raymond Lopez. Raymond Lopez, no. No, Nicola Rocca. Raymond went up there too. Nicola Rocca was with the... Before Nicola Rocca got it. Did Vega ever go anywhere?
No, Vega died before that started.

Lawrence died. Was he good young? Yeah, he was good young. Was he a technician or a hot man? Hot man. Hot man. Very hot. Who's that? There was only three hot men there. Lawrence Vega. Lawrence Vega. There was only three hot men in town at that time. With me, Emil Christian and Lawrence Vega. The rest... Emil played trumpet a lot. Yeah, he played trumpet, yeah. Emil played trumpet, yeah. What year would that have been in, John? Oh, 1910. Do you remember... 1912.
